questions.q: What is the primary purpose of this practice lab lesson?
options: To apply the whole course's design sequence end to end on a scenario the student chooses themselves
To introduce several brand-new governance concepts not covered earlier in the course
To grade students against a fixed, single correct answer
To replace the need for Chapters 1 through 5 entirely
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit: no new concepts, just building the skill of applying everything already taught to a real scenario.

questions.q: If a student chooses a fictional organization for this exercise, what does the lesson require?
options: That it be clearly labeled fictional, ideally in a different industry than Castellan or Northbridge
That it be presented as a real, named company
That it must be based on a real competitor of the student's employer
That no scenario details be written down at all
questions.explain: The lesson requires fictional scenarios to be clearly labeled as such, and suggests a different industry for better practice.

questions.q: Which of these is one of the seven steps in this lesson's design checklist?
options: An operating model choice with a one-sentence reason tied to the scenario
Selecting a company logo and color palette
Hiring a new executive assistant
Filing a patent application
questions.explain: Step 2 of the checklist is choosing an operating model (centralized, federated, decentralized, data mesh, or hybrid) with a stated reason.

questions.q: Per the lesson, what distinguishes a complete design package from an incomplete one?
options: Every step has a specific answer tied to the chosen scenario, not a restatement of generic course definitions
It must be at least twenty pages long
It must include a professionally designed slide deck
It must name a real company by name
questions.explain: The lesson's self-review instruction is explicit: check for genuine specificity tied to the scenario, not generic restated definitions.

questions.q: What does the final lesson of the course, covered next, focus on?
options: Presenting a finished governance architecture to stakeholders
Installing a specific database management system
Writing a resignation letter
Configuring a firewall rule set
questions.explain: Lesson 30, Presenting Governance Architecture, is the course's closing lesson on communicating this work to stakeholders.
